title: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology

source.catalogTitle: Electronic Version of NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0

groups.title: Govern
groups.description: The organization's cybersecurity risk management strategy, expectations, and policy are established, communicated, and monitored

groups.title: Organizational Context
groups.description: The circumstances - mission, stakeholder expectations, dependencies, and legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements - surrounding the organization's cybersecurity risk management decisions are understood

groups.title: Risk Management Strategy
groups.description: The organization's priorities, constraints, risk tolerance and appetite statements, and assumptions are established, communicated, and used to support operational risk decisions

groups.title: Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities
groups.description: Cybersecurity roles, responsibilities, and authorities to foster accountability, performance assessment, and continuous improvement are established and communicated

groups.title: Policy
groups.description: Organizational cybersecurity policy is established, communicated, and enforced

groups.title: Oversight
groups.description: Results of organization-wide cybersecurity risk management activities and performance are used to inform, improve, and adjust the risk management strategy

groups.title: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management
groups.description: Cyber supply chain risk management processes are identified, established, managed, monitored, and improved by organizational stakeholders

groups.title: Identify
groups.description: The organization's current cybersecurity risks are understood

groups.title: Asset Management
groups.description: Assets (e.g., data, hardware, software, systems, facilities, services, people) that enable the organization to achieve business purposes are identified and managed consistent with their relative importance to organizational objectives and the organization's risk strategy

groups.title: Risk Assessment
groups.description: The cybersecurity risk to the organization, assets, and individuals is understood by the organization

groups.title: Improvement
groups.description: Improvements to organizational cybersecurity risk management processes, procedures and activities are identified across all CSF Functions

groups.title: Protect
groups.description: Safeguards to manage the organization's cybersecurity risks are used

groups.title: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
groups.description: Access to physical and logical assets is limited to authorized users, services, and hardware and managed commensurate with the assessed risk of unauthorized access

groups.title: Awareness and Training
groups.description: The organization's personnel are provided with cybersecurity awareness and training so that they can perform their cybersecurity-related tasks

groups.title: Data Security
groups.description: Data are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information

groups.title: Platform Security
groups.description: The hardware, software (e.g., firmware, operating systems, applications), and services of physical and virtual platforms are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect their confidentiality, integrity, and availability

groups.title: Technology Infrastructure Resilience
groups.description: Security architectures are managed with the organization's risk strategy to protect asset confidentiality, integrity, and availability, and organizational resilience

groups.title: Detect
groups.description: Possible cybersecurity attacks and compromises are found and analyzed

groups.title: Adverse Event Analysis
groups.description: Anomalies, indicators of compromise, and other potentially adverse events are analyzed to characterize the events and detect cybersecurity incidents

groups.title: Continuous Monitoring
groups.description: Assets are monitored to find anomalies, indicators of compromise, and other potentially adverse events

groups.title: Respond
groups.description: Actions regarding a detected cybersecurity incident are taken

groups.title: Incident Management
groups.description: Responses to detected cybersecurity incidents are managed

groups.title: Incident Analysis
groups.description: Investigations are conducted to ensure effective response and support forensics and recovery activities

groups.title: Incident Response Reporting and Communication
groups.description: Response activities are coordinated with internal and external stakeholders as required by laws, regulations, or policies

groups.title: Incident Mitigation
groups.description: Activities are performed to prevent expansion of an event and mitigate its effects

groups.title: Recover
groups.description: Assets and operations affected by a cybersecurity incident are restored

groups.title: Incident Recovery Plan Execution
groups.description: Restoration activities are performed to ensure operational availability of systems and services affected by cybersecurity incidents

groups.title: Incident Recovery Communication
groups.description: Restoration activities are coordinated with internal and external parties

requirements.title: The organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management

statement.text: The organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Share the organization's mission (e.g., through vision and mission statements, marketing, and service strategies) to provide a basis for identifying risks that may impede that mission

requirements.title: Internal and external stakeholders are understood, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood and considered

statement.text: Internal and external stakeholders are understood, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood and considered

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Identify relevant internal stakeholders and their cybersecurity-related expectations (e.g., performance and risk expectations of officers, directors, and advisors; cultural expectations of employees)

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Identify relevant external stakeholders and their cybersecurity-related expectations (e.g., privacy expectations of customers, business expectations of partnerships, compliance expectations of regulators, ethics expectations of society)

requirements.title: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity - including privacy and civil liberties obligations - are understood and managed

statement.text: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity - including privacy and civil liberties obligations - are understood and managed

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Determine a process to track and manage legal and regulatory requirements regarding protection of individuals' information (e.g., Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, California Consumer Privacy Act, General Data Protection Regulation)

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Determine a process to track and manage contractual requirements for cybersecurity management of supplier, customer, and partner information

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Align the organization's cybersecurity strategy with legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements

requirements.title: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the organization are understood and communicated

statement.text: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the organization are understood and communicated

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Establish criteria for determining the criticality of capabilities and services as viewed by internal and external stakeholders

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Determine (e.g., from a business impact analysis) assets and business operations that are vital to achieving mission objectives and the potential impact of a loss (or partial loss) of such operations

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Establish and communicate resilience objectives (e.g., recovery time objectives) for delivering critical capabilities and services in various operating states (e.g., under attack, during recovery, normal operation)

requirements.title: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organization depends on are understood and communicated

statement.text: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organization depends on are understood and communicated

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Create an inventory of the organization's dependencies on external resources (e.g., facilities, cloud-based hosting providers) and their relationships to organizational assets and business functions

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Identify and document external dependencies that are potential points of failure for the organization's critical capabilities and services, and share that information with appropriate personnel

requirements.title: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders

statement.text: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Update near-term and long-term cybersecurity risk management objectives as part of annual strategic planning and when major changes occur

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Establish measurable objectives for cybersecurity risk management (e.g., manage the quality of user training, ensure adequate risk protection for industrial control systems)

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Senior leaders agree about cybersecurity objectives and use them for measuring and managing risk and performance

requirements.title: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained

statement.text: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Determine and communicate risk appetite statements that convey expectations about the appropriate level of risk for the organization

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Translate risk appetite statements into specific, measurable, and broadly understandable risk tolerance statements

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Refine organizational objectives and risk appetite periodically based on known risk exposure and residual risk

requirements.title: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes

statement.text: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Aggregate and manage cybersecurity risks alongside other enterprise risks (e.g., compliance, financial, operational, regulatory, reputational, safety)

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Include cybersecurity risk managers in enterprise risk management planning

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Establish criteria for escalating cybersecurity risks within enterprise risk management

requirements.title: Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated

statement.text: Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Specify criteria for accepting and avoiding cybersecurity risk for various classifications of data

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Determine whether to purchase cybersecurity insurance

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Document conditions under which shared responsibility models are acceptable (e.g., outsourcing certain cybersecurity functions, having a third party perform financial transactions on behalf of the organization, using public cloud-based services)

requirements.title: Lines of communication across the organization are established for cybersecurity risks, including risks from suppliers and other third parties

statement.text: Lines of communication across the organization are established for cybersecurity risks, including risks from suppliers and other third parties

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Determine how to update senior executives, directors, and management on the organization's cybersecurity posture at agreed-upon intervals

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Identify how all departments across the organization - such as management, operations, internal auditors, legal, acquisition, physical security, and HR - will communicate with each other about cybersecurity risks

requirements.title: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing, and prioritizing cybersecurity risks is established and communicated

statement.text: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing, and prioritizing cybersecurity risks is established and communicated

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Establish criteria for using a quantitative approach to cybersecurity risk analysis, and specify probability and exposure formulas

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Create and use templates (e.g., a risk register) to document cybersecurity risk information (e.g., risk description, exposure, treatment, and ownership)

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Establish criteria for risk prioritization at the appropriate levels within the enterprise

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Use a consistent list of risk categories to support integrating, aggregating, and comparing cybersecurity risks

requirements.title: Strategic opportunities (i.e., positive risks) are characterized and are included in organizational cybersecurity risk discussions

statement.text: Strategic opportunities (i.e., positive risks) are characterized and are included in organizational cybersecurity risk discussions

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Define and communicate guidance and methods for identifying opportunities and including them in risk discussions (e.g., strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT) analysis)

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Identify stretch goals and document them

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Calculate, document, and prioritize positive risks alongside negative risks

requirements.title: Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture that is risk-aware, ethical, and continually improving

statement.text: Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture that is risk-aware, ethical, and continually improving

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Leaders (e.g., directors) agree on their roles and responsibilities in developing, implementing, and assessing the organization's cybersecurity strategy

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Share leaders' expectations regarding a secure and ethical culture, especially when current events present the opportunity to highlight positive or negative examples of cybersecurity risk management

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Leaders direct the CISO to maintain a comprehensive cybersecurity risk strategy and review and update it at least annually and after major events

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Conduct reviews to ensure adequate authority and coordination among those responsible for managing cybersecurity risk

requirements.title: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced

statement.text: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Document risk management roles and responsibilities in policy

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Document who is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk management activities and how those teams and individuals are to be consulted and informed

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Include cybersecurity responsibilities and performance requirements in personnel descriptions

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Document performance goals for personnel with cybersecurity risk management responsibilities, and periodically measure performance to identify areas for improvement

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Clearly articulate cybersecurity responsibilities within operations, risk functions, and internal audit functions

requirements.title: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with the cybersecurity risk strategy, roles, responsibilities, and policies

statement.text: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with the cybersecurity risk strategy, roles, responsibilities, and policies

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Conduct periodic management reviews to ensure that those given cybersecurity risk management responsibilities have the necessary authority

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Identify resource allocation and investment in line with risk tolerance and response

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Provide adequate and sufficient people, process, and technical resources to support the cybersecurity strategy

requirements.title: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices

statement.text: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Integrate cybersecurity risk management considerations into human resources processes (e.g., personnel screening, onboarding, change notification, offboarding)

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Consider cybersecurity knowledge to be a positive factor in hiring, training, and retention decisions

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Conduct background checks prior to onboarding new personnel for sensitive roles, and periodically repeat background checks for personnel with such roles

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Define and enforce obligations for personnel to be aware of, adhere to, and uphold security policies as they relate to their roles

requirements.title: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced

statement.text: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Create, disseminate, and maintain an understandable, usable risk management policy with statements of management intent, expectations, and direction

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Periodically review policy and supporting processes and procedures to ensure that they align with risk management strategy objectives and priorities, as well as the high-level direction of the cybersecurity policy

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Require approval from senior management on policy

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Communicate cybersecurity risk management policy and supporting processes and procedures across the organization

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Require personnel to acknowledge receipt of policy when first hired, annually, and whenever policy is updated

requirements.title: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and organizational mission

statement.text: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and organizational mission

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Update policy based on periodic reviews of cybersecurity risk management results to ensure that policy and supporting processes and procedures adequately maintain risk at an acceptable level

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Provide a timeline for reviewing changes to the organization's risk environment (e.g., changes in risk or in the organization's mission objectives), and communicate recommended policy updates

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Update policy to reflect changes in legal and regulatory requirements

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Update policy to reflect changes in technology (e.g., adoption of artificial intelligence) and changes to the business (e.g., acquisition of a new business, new contract requirements)

requirements.title: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction

statement.text: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Measure how well the risk management strategy and risk results have helped leaders make decisions and achieve organizational objectives

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Examine whether cybersecurity risk strategies that impede operations or innovation should be adjusted

requirements.title: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organizational requirements and risks

statement.text: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organizational requirements and risks

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Review audit findings to confirm whether the existing cybersecurity strategy has ensured compliance with internal and external requirements

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Review the performance oversight of those in cybersecurity-related roles to determine whether policy changes are necessary

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Review strategy in light of cybersecurity incidents

requirements.title: Organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed

statement.text: Organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Review key performance indicators (KPIs) to ensure that organization-wide policies and procedures achieve objectives

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Review key risk indicators (KRIs) to identify risks the organization faces, including likelihood and potential impact

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Collect and communicate metrics on cybersecurity risk management with senior leadership

requirements.title: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders

statement.text: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Establish a strategy that expresses the objectives of the cybersecurity supply chain risk management program

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Develop the cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, including a plan (with milestones), policies, and procedures that guide implementation and improvement of the program, and share the policies and procedures with the organizational stakeholders

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Develop and implement program processes based on the strategy, objectives, policies, and procedures that are agreed upon and performed by the organizational stakeholders

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Establish a cross-organizational mechanism that ensures alignment between functions that contribute to cybersecurity supply chain risk management, such as cybersecurity, IT, operations, legal, human resources, and engineering

requirements.title: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally

statement.text: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Identify one or more specific roles or positions that will be responsible and accountable for planning, resourcing, and executing cybersecurity supply chain risk management activities

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Document cybersecurity supply chain risk management roles and responsibilities in policy

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Create responsibility matrixes to document who will be responsible and accountable for cybersecurity supply chain risk management activities and how those teams and individuals will be consulted and informed

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Include cybersecurity supply chain risk management responsibilities and performance requirements in personnel descriptions to ensure clarity and improve accountability

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Document performance goals for personnel with cybersecurity risk management-specific responsibilities, and periodically measure them to demonstrate and improve performance

examples.label: Ex6
examples.text: Develop roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and business partners to address shared responsibilities for applicable cybersecurity risks, and integrate them into organizational policies and applicable third-party agreements

examples.label: Ex7
examples.text: Internally communicate cybersecurity supply chain risk management roles and responsibilities for third parties

examples.label: Ex8
examples.text: Establish rules and protocols for information sharing and reporting processes between the organization and its suppliers

requirements.title: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management, risk assessment, and improvement processes

statement.text: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management, risk assessment, and improvement processes

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Identify areas of alignment and overlap with cybersecurity and enterprise risk management

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Establish integrated control sets for cybersecurity risk management and cybersecurity supply chain risk management

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Integrate cybersecurity supply chain risk management into improvement processes

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Escalate material cybersecurity risks in supply chains to senior management, and address them at the enterprise risk management level

requirements.title: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality

statement.text: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Develop criteria for supplier criticality based on, for example, the sensitivity of data processed or possessed by suppliers, the degree of access to the organization's systems, and the importance of the products or services to the organization's mission

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Keep a record of all suppliers, and prioritize suppliers based on the criticality criteria

requirements.title: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other types of agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties

statement.text: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other types of agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Establish security requirements for suppliers, products, and services commensurate with their criticality level and potential impact if compromised

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Include all cybersecurity and supply chain requirements that third parties must follow and how compliance with the requirements may be verified in default contractual language

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Define the rules and protocols for information sharing between the organization and its suppliers and sub-tier suppliers in agreements

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Manage risk by including security requirements in agreements based on their criticality and potential impact if compromised

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Define security requirements in service-level agreements (SLAs) for monitoring suppliers for acceptable security performance throughout the supplier relationship lifecycle

examples.label: Ex6
examples.text: Contractually require suppliers to disclose cybersecurity features, functions, and vulnerabilities of their products and services for the life of the product or the term of service

examples.label: Ex7
examples.text: Contractually require suppliers to provide and maintain a current component inventory (e.g., software or hardware bill of materials) for critical products

examples.label: Ex8
examples.text: Contractually require suppliers to vet their employees and guard against insider threats

examples.label: Ex9
examples.text: Contractually require suppliers to provide evidence of performing acceptable security practices through, for example, self-attestation, conformance to known standards, certifications, or inspections

examples.label: Ex10
examples.text: Specify in contracts and other agreements the rights and responsibilities of the organization, its suppliers, and their supply chains, with respect to potential cybersecurity risks

requirements.title: Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into formal supplier or other third-party relationships

statement.text: Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into formal supplier or other third-party relationships

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Perform thorough due diligence on prospective suppliers that is consistent with procurement planning and commensurate with the level of risk, criticality, and complexity of each supplier relationship

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Assess the suitability of the technology and cybersecurity capabilities and the risk management practices of prospective suppliers

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Conduct supplier risk assessments against business and applicable cybersecurity requirements

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Assess the authenticity, integrity, and security of critical products prior to acquisition and use

requirements.title: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are understood, recorded, prioritized, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship

statement.text: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are understood, recorded, prioritized, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Adjust assessment formats and frequencies based on the third party's reputation and the criticality of the products or services they provide

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Evaluate third parties' evidence of compliance with contractual cybersecurity requirements, such as self-attestations, warranties, certifications, and other artifacts

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Monitor critical suppliers to ensure that they are fulfilling their security obligations throughout the supplier relationship lifecycle using a variety of methods and techniques, such as inspections, audits, tests, or other forms of evaluation

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Monitor critical suppliers, services, and products for changes to their risk profiles, and reevaluate supplier criticality and risk impact accordingly

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Plan for unexpected supplier and supply chain-related interruptions to ensure business continuity

requirements.title: Relevant suppliers and other third parties are included in incident planning, response, and recovery activities

statement.text: Relevant suppliers and other third parties are included in incident planning, response, and recovery activities

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Define and use rules and protocols for reporting incident response and recovery activities and the status between the organization and its suppliers

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Identify and document the roles and responsibilities of the organization and its suppliers for incident response

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Include critical suppliers in incident response exercises and simulations

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Define and coordinate crisis communication methods and protocols between the organization and its critical suppliers

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Conduct collaborative lessons learned sessions with critical suppliers

requirements.title: Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programs, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle

statement.text: Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programs, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Policies and procedures require provenance records for all acquired technology products and services

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Periodically provide risk reporting to leaders about how acquired components are proven to be untampered and authentic

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Communicate regularly among cybersecurity risk managers and operations personnel about the need to acquire software patches, updates, and upgrades only from authenticated and trustworthy software providers

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Review policies to ensure that they require approved supplier personnel to perform maintenance on supplier products

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Policies and procedure require checking upgrades to critical hardware for unauthorized changes

requirements.title: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management plans include provisions for activities that occur after the conclusion of a partnership or service agreement

statement.text: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management plans include provisions for activities that occur after the conclusion of a partnership or service agreement

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Establish processes for terminating critical relationships under both normal and adverse circumstances

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Define and implement plans for component end-of-life maintenance support and obsolescence

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Verify that supplier access to organization resources is deactivated promptly when it is no longer needed

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Verify that assets containing the organization's data are returned or properly disposed of in a timely, controlled, and safe manner

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Develop and execute a plan for terminating or transitioning supplier relationships that takes supply chain security risk and resiliency into account

examples.label: Ex6
examples.text: Mitigate risks to data and systems created by supplier termination

examples.label: Ex7
examples.text: Manage data leakage risks associated with supplier termination

requirements.title: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained

statement.text: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Maintain inventories for all types of hardware, including IT, IoT, OT, and mobile devices

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Constantly monitor networks to detect new hardware and automatically update inventories

requirements.title: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained

statement.text: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Maintain inventories for all types of software and services, including commercial-off-the-shelf, open-source, custom applications, API services, and cloud-based applications and services

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Constantly monitor all platforms, including containers and virtual machines, for software and service inventory changes

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Maintain an inventory of the organization's systems

requirements.title: Representations of the organization's authorized network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained

statement.text: Representations of the organization's authorized network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Maintain baselines of communication and data flows within the organization's wired and wireless networks

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Maintain baselines of communication and data flows between the organization and third parties

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Maintain baselines of communication and data flows for the organization's infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) usage

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Maintain documentation of expected network ports, protocols, and services that are typically used among authorized systems

requirements.title: Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained

statement.text: Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Inventory all external services used by the organization, including third-party infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS), platform-as-a-service (PaaS), and software-as-a-service (SaaS) offerings; APIs; and other externally hosted application services

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Update the inventory when a new external service is going to be utilized to ensure adequate cybersecurity risk management monitoring of the organization's use of that service

requirements.title: Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission

statement.text: Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Define criteria for prioritizing each class of assets

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Apply the prioritization criteria to assets

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Track the asset priorities and update them periodically or when significant changes to the organization occur

requirements.title: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained

statement.text: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Maintain a list of the designated data types of interest (e.g., personally identifiable information, protected health information, financial account numbers, organization intellectual property, operational technology data)

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Continuously discover and analyze ad hoc data to identify new instances of designated data types

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Assign data classifications to designated data types through tags or labels

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Track the provenance, data owner, and geolocation of each instance of designated data types

requirements.title: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles

statement.text: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Integrate cybersecurity considerations throughout the life cycles of systems, hardware, software, and services

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Integrate cybersecurity considerations into product life cycles

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Identify unofficial uses of technology to meet mission objectives (i.e., shadow IT)

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Periodically identify redundant systems, hardware, software, and services that unnecessarily increase the organization's attack surface

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Properly configure and secure systems, hardware, software, and services prior to their deployment in production

examples.label: Ex6
examples.text: Update inventories when systems, hardware, software, and services are moved or transferred within the organization

examples.label: Ex7
examples.text: Securely destroy stored data based on the organization's data retention policy using the prescribed destruction method, and keep and manage a record of the destructions

examples.label: Ex8
examples.text: Securely sanitize data storage when hardware is being retired, decommissioned, reassigned, or sent for repairs or replacement

examples.label: Ex9
examples.text: Offer methods for destroying paper, storage media, and other physical forms of data storage

requirements.title: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded

statement.text: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Use vulnerability management technologies to identify unpatched and misconfigured software

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Assess network and system architectures for design and implementation weaknesses that affect cybersecurity

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Review, analyze, or test organization-developed software to identify design, coding, and default configuration vulnerabilities

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Assess facilities that house critical computing assets for physical vulnerabilities and resilience issues

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Monitor sources of cyber threat intelligence for information on new vulnerabilities in products and services

examples.label: Ex6
examples.text: Review processes and procedures for weaknesses that could be exploited to affect cybersecurity

requirements.title: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources

statement.text: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Configure cybersecurity tools and technologies with detection or response capabilities to securely ingest cyber threat intelligence feeds

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Receive and review advisories from reputable third parties on current threat actors and their tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs)

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Monitor sources of cyber threat intelligence for information on the types of vulnerabilities that emerging technologies may have

requirements.title: Internal and external threats to the organization are identified and recorded

statement.text: Internal and external threats to the organization are identified and recorded

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Use cyber threat intelligence to maintain awareness of the types of threat actors likely to target the organization and the TTPs they are likely to use

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Perform threat hunting to look for signs of threat actors within the environment

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Implement processes for identifying internal threat actors

requirements.title: Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded

statement.text: Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Business leaders and cybersecurity risk management practitioners work together to estimate the likelihood and impact of risk scenarios and record them in risk registers

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Enumerate the potential business impacts of unauthorized access to the organization's communications, systems, and data processed in or by those systems

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Account for the potential impacts of cascading failures for systems of systems

requirements.title: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization

statement.text: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Develop threat models to better understand risks to the data and identify appropriate risk responses

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Prioritize cybersecurity resource allocations and investments based on estimated likelihoods and impacts

requirements.title: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked, and communicated

statement.text: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked, and communicated

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Apply the vulnerability management plan's criteria for deciding whether to accept, transfer, mitigate, or avoid risk

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Apply the vulnerability management plan's criteria for selecting compensating controls to mitigate risk

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Track the progress of risk response implementation (e.g., plan of action and milestones (POA&M), risk register, risk detail report)

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Use risk assessment findings to inform risk response decisions and actions

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Communicate planned risk responses to affected stakeholders in priority order

requirements.title: Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, recorded, and tracked

statement.text: Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, recorded, and tracked

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Implement and follow procedures for the formal documentation, review, testing, and approval of proposed changes and requested exceptions

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Document the possible risks of making or not making each proposed change, and provide guidance on rolling back changes

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Document the risks related to each requested exception and the plan for responding to those risks

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Periodically review risks that were accepted based upon planned future actions or milestones

requirements.title: Processes for receiving, analyzing, and responding to vulnerability disclosures are established

statement.text: Processes for receiving, analyzing, and responding to vulnerability disclosures are established

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Conduct vulnerability information sharing between the organization and its suppliers following the rules and protocols defined in contracts

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Assign responsibilities and verify the execution of procedures for processing, analyzing the impact of, and responding to cybersecurity threat, vulnerability, or incident disclosures by suppliers, customers, partners, and government cybersecurity organizations

requirements.title: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use

statement.text: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Assess the authenticity and cybersecurity of critical technology products and services prior to acquisition and use

requirements.title: Critical suppliers are assessed prior to acquisition

statement.text: Critical suppliers are assessed prior to acquisition

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Conduct supplier risk assessments against business and applicable cybersecurity requirements, including the supply chain

requirements.title: Improvements are identified from evaluations

statement.text: Improvements are identified from evaluations

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Perform self-assessments of critical services that take current threats and TTPs into consideration

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Invest in third-party assessments or independent audits of the effectiveness of the organization's cybersecurity program to identify areas that need improvement

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Constantly evaluate compliance with selected cybersecurity requirements through automated means

requirements.title: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and relevant third parties

statement.text: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and relevant third parties

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Identify improvements for future incident response activities based on findings from incident response assessments (e.g., tabletop exercises and simulations, tests, internal reviews, independent audits)

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Identify improvements for future business continuity, disaster recovery, and incident response activities based on exercises performed in coordination with critical service providers and product suppliers

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Involve internal stakeholders (e.g., senior executives, legal department, HR) in security tests and exercises as appropriate

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Perform penetration testing to identify opportunities to improve the security posture of selected high-risk systems as approved by leadership

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Exercise contingency plans for responding to and recovering from the discovery that products or services did not originate with the contracted supplier or partner or were altered before receipt

examples.label: Ex6
examples.text: Collect and analyze performance metrics using security tools and services to inform improvements to the cybersecurity program

requirements.title: Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities

statement.text: Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Conduct collaborative lessons learned sessions with suppliers

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Annually review cybersecurity policies, processes, and procedures to take lessons learned into account

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Use metrics to assess operational cybersecurity performance over time

requirements.title: Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained, and improved

statement.text: Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained, and improved

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Establish contingency plans (e.g., incident response, business continuity, disaster recovery) for responding to and recovering from adverse events that can interfere with operations, expose confidential information, or otherwise endanger the organization's mission and viability

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Include contact and communication information, processes for handling common scenarios, and criteria for prioritization, escalation, and elevation in all contingency plans

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Create a vulnerability management plan to identify and assess all types of vulnerabilities and to prioritize, test, and implement risk responses

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Communicate cybersecurity plans (including updates) to those responsible for carrying them out and to affected parties

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Review and update all cybersecurity plans annually or when a need for significant improvements is identified

requirements.title: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization

statement.text: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Initiate requests for new access or additional access for employees, contractors, and others, and track, review, and fulfill the requests, with permission from system or data owners when needed

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Issue, manage, and revoke cryptographic certificates and identity tokens, cryptographic keys (i.e., key management), and other credentials

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Select a unique identifier for each device from immutable hardware characteristics or an identifier securely provisioned to the device

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Physically label authorized hardware with an identifier for inventory and servicing purposes

requirements.title: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions

statement.text: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Verify a person's claimed identity at enrollment time using government-issued identity credentials (e.g., passport, visa, driver's license)

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Issue a different credential for each person (i.e., no credential sharing)

requirements.title: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated

statement.text: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Require multifactor authentication

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Enforce policies for the minimum strength of passwords, PINs, and similar authenticators

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Periodically reauthenticate users, services, and hardware based on risk (e.g., in zero trust architectures)

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Ensure that authorized personnel can access accounts essential for protecting safety under emergency conditions

requirements.title: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified

statement.text: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Protect identity assertions that are used to convey authentication and user information through single sign-on systems

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Protect identity assertions that are used to convey authentication and user information between federated systems

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Implement standards-based approaches for identity assertions in all contexts, and follow all guidance for the generation (e.g., data models, metadata), protection (e.g., digital signing, encryption), and verification (e.g., signature validation) of identity assertions

requirements.title: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties

statement.text: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Review logical and physical access privileges periodically and whenever someone changes roles or leaves the organization, and promptly rescind privileges that are no longer needed

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Take attributes of the requester and the requested resource into account for authorization decisions (e.g., geolocation, day/time, requester endpoint's cyber health)

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Restrict access and privileges to the minimum necessary (e.g., zero trust architecture)

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Periodically review the privileges associated with critical business functions to confirm proper separation of duties

requirements.title: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored, and enforced commensurate with risk

statement.text: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored, and enforced commensurate with risk

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Use security guards, security cameras, locked entrances, alarm systems, and other physical controls to monitor facilities and restrict access

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Employ additional physical security controls for areas that contain high-risk assets

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Escort guests, vendors, and other third parties within areas that contain business-critical assets

requirements.title: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform general tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind

statement.text: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform general tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Provide basic cybersecurity awareness and training to employees, contractors, partners, suppliers, and all other users of the organization's non-public resources

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Train personnel to recognize social engineering attempts and other common attacks, report attacks and suspicious activity, comply with acceptable use policies, and perform basic cyber hygiene tasks (e.g., patching software, choosing passwords, protecting credentials)

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Explain the consequences of cybersecurity policy violations, both to individual users and the organization as a whole

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Periodically assess or test users on their understanding of basic cybersecurity practices

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Require annual refreshers to reinforce existing practices and introduce new practices

requirements.title: Individuals in specialized roles are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform relevant tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind

statement.text: Individuals in specialized roles are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform relevant tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Identify the specialized roles within the organization that require additional cybersecurity training, such as physical and cybersecurity personnel, finance personnel, senior leadership, and anyone with access to business-critical data

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Provide role-based cybersecurity awareness and training to all those in specialized roles, including contractors, partners, suppliers, and other third parties

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Periodically assess or test users on their understanding of cybersecurity practices for their specialized roles

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Require annual refreshers to reinforce existing practices and introduce new practices

requirements.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected

statement.text: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Use encryption, digital signatures, and cryptographic hashes to protect the confidentiality and integrity of stored data in files, databases, virtual machine disk images, container images, and other resources

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Use full disk encryption to protect data stored on user endpoints

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Confirm the integrity of software by validating signatures

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Restrict the use of removable media to prevent data exfiltration

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Physically secure removable media containing unencrypted sensitive information, such as within locked offices or file cabinets

requirements.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected

statement.text: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Use encryption, digital signatures, and cryptographic hashes to protect the confidentiality and integrity of network communications

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Automatically encrypt or block outbound emails and other communications that contain sensitive data, depending on the data classification

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Block access to personal email, file sharing, file storage services, and other personal communications applications and services from organizational systems and networks

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Prevent reuse of sensitive data from production environments (e.g., customer records) in development, testing, and other non-production environments

requirements.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected

statement.text: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Remove data that must remain confidential (e.g., from processors and memory) as soon as it is no longer needed

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Protect data in use from access by other users and processes of the same platform

requirements.title: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested

statement.text: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Continuously back up critical data in near-real-time, and back up other data frequently at agreed-upon schedules

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Test backups and restores for all types of data sources at least annually

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Securely store some backups offline and offsite so that an incident or disaster will not damage them

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Enforce geographic separation and geolocation restrictions for data backup storage

requirements.title: Configuration management practices are established and applied

statement.text: Configuration management practices are established and applied

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Establish, test, deploy, and maintain hardened baselines that enforce the organization's cybersecurity policies and provide only essential capabilities (i.e., principle of least functionality)

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Review all default configuration settings that may potentially impact cybersecurity when installing or upgrading software

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Monitor implemented software for deviations from approved baselines

requirements.title: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk

statement.text: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Perform routine and emergency patching within the timeframes specified in the vulnerability management plan

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Update container images, and deploy new container instances to replace rather than update existing instances

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Replace end-of-life software and service versions with supported, maintained versions

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Uninstall and remove unauthorized software and services that pose undue risks

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Uninstall and remove any unnecessary software components (e.g., operating system utilities) that attackers might misuse

examples.label: Ex6
examples.text: Define and implement plans for software and service end-of-life maintenance support and obsolescence

requirements.title: Hardware is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk

statement.text: Hardware is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Replace hardware when it lacks needed security capabilities or when it cannot support software with needed security capabilities

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Define and implement plans for hardware end-of-life maintenance support and obsolescence

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Perform hardware disposal in a secure, responsible, and auditable manner

requirements.title: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring

statement.text: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Configure all operating systems, applications, and services (including cloud-based services) to generate log records

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Configure log generators to securely share their logs with the organization's logging infrastructure systems and services

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Configure log generators to record the data needed by zero-trust architectures

requirements.title: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented

statement.text: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: When risk warrants it, restrict software execution to permitted products only or deny the execution of prohibited and unauthorized software

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Verify the source of new software and the software's integrity before installing it

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Configure platforms to use only approved DNS services that block access to known malicious domains

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Configure platforms to allow the installation of organization-approved software only

requirements.title: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle

statement.text: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Protect all components of organization-developed software from tampering and unauthorized access

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Secure all software produced by the organization, with minimal vulnerabilities in their releases

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Maintain the software used in production environments, and securely dispose of software once it is no longer needed

requirements.title: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage

statement.text: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Logically segment organization networks and cloud-based platforms according to trust boundaries and platform types (e.g., IT, IoT, OT, mobile, guests), and permit required communications only between segments

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Logically segment organization networks from external networks, and permit only necessary communications to enter the organization's networks from the external networks

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Implement zero trust architectures to restrict network access to each resource to the minimum necessary

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Check the cyber health of endpoints before allowing them to access and use production resources

requirements.title: The organization's technology assets are protected from environmental threats

statement.text: The organization's technology assets are protected from environmental threats

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Protect organizational equipment from known environmental threats, such as flooding, fire, wind, and excessive heat and humidity

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Include protection from environmental threats and provisions for adequate operating infrastructure in requirements for service providers that operate systems on the organization's behalf

requirements.title: Mechanisms are implemented to achieve resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations

statement.text: Mechanisms are implemented to achieve resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Avoid single points of failure in systems and infrastructure

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Use load balancing to increase capacity and improve reliability

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Use high-availability components like redundant storage and power supplies to improve system reliability

requirements.title: Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained

statement.text: Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Monitor usage of storage, power, compute, network bandwidth, and other resources

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Forecast future needs, and scale resources accordingly

requirements.title: Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better understand associated activities

statement.text: Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better understand associated activities

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Use security information and event management (SIEM) or other tools to continuously monitor log events for known malicious and suspicious activity

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Utilize up-to-date cyber threat intelligence in log analysis tools to improve detection accuracy and characterize threat actors, their methods, and indicators of compromise

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Regularly conduct manual reviews of log events for technologies that cannot be sufficiently monitored through automation

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Use log analysis tools to generate reports on their findings

requirements.title: Information is correlated from multiple sources

statement.text: Information is correlated from multiple sources

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Constantly transfer log data generated by other sources to a relatively small number of log servers

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Use event correlation technology (e.g., SIEM) to collect information captured by multiple sources

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Utilize cyber threat intelligence to help correlate events among log sources

requirements.title: The estimated impact and scope of adverse events are understood

statement.text: The estimated impact and scope of adverse events are understood

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Use SIEMs or other tools to estimate impact and scope, and review and refine the estimates

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: A person creates their own estimates of impact and scope

requirements.title: Information on adverse events is provided to authorized staff and tools

statement.text: Information on adverse events is provided to authorized staff and tools

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Use cybersecurity software to generate alerts and provide them to the security operations center (SOC), incident responders, and incident response tools

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Incident responders and other authorized personnel can access log analysis findings at all times

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Automatically create and assign tickets in the organization's ticketing system when certain types of alerts occur

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Manually create and assign tickets in the organization's ticketing system when technical staff discover indicators of compromise

requirements.title: Cyber threat intelligence and other contextual information are integrated into the analysis

statement.text: Cyber threat intelligence and other contextual information are integrated into the analysis

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Securely provide cyber threat intelligence feeds to detection technologies, processes, and personnel

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Securely provide information from asset inventories to detection technologies, processes, and personnel

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Rapidly acquire and analyze vulnerability disclosures for the organization's technologies from suppliers, vendors, and third-party security advisories

requirements.title: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria

statement.text: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Apply incident criteria to known and assumed characteristics of activity in order to determine whether an incident should be declared

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Take known false positives into account when applying incident criteria

requirements.title: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events

statement.text: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Monitor DNS, BGP, and other network services for adverse events

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Monitor wired and wireless networks for connections from unauthorized endpoints

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Monitor facilities for unauthorized or rogue wireless networks

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Compare actual network flows against baselines to detect deviations

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Monitor network communications to identify changes in security postures for zero trust purposes

requirements.title: The physical environment is monitored to find potentially adverse events

statement.text: The physical environment is monitored to find potentially adverse events

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Monitor logs from physical access control systems (e.g., badge readers) to find unusual access patterns (e.g., deviations from the norm) and failed access attempts

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Review and monitor physical access records (e.g., from visitor registration, sign-in sheets)

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Monitor physical access controls (e.g., locks, latches, hinge pins, alarms) for signs of tampering

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Monitor the physical environment using alarm systems, cameras, and security guards

requirements.title: Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events

statement.text: Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Use behavior analytics software to detect anomalous user activity to mitigate insider threats

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Monitor logs from logical access control systems to find unusual access patterns and failed access attempts

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Continuously monitor deception technology, including user accounts, for any usage

requirements.title: External service provider activities and services are monitored to find potentially adverse events

statement.text: External service provider activities and services are monitored to find potentially adverse events

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Monitor remote and onsite administration and maintenance activities that external providers perform on organizational systems

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Monitor activity from cloud-based services, internet service providers, and other service providers for deviations from expected behavior

requirements.title: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events

statement.text: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Monitor email, web, file sharing, collaboration services, and other common attack vectors to detect malware, phishing, data leaks and exfiltration, and other adverse events

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Monitor authentication attempts to identify attacks against credentials and unauthorized credential reuse

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Monitor software configurations for deviations from security baselines

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Monitor hardware and software for signs of tampering

examples.label: Ex5
examples.text: Use technologies with a presence on endpoints to detect cyber health issues (e.g., missing patches, malware infections, unauthorized software), and redirect the endpoints to a remediation environment before access is authorized

requirements.title: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared

statement.text: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Detection technologies automatically report confirmed incidents

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Request incident response assistance from the organization's incident response outsourcer

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Designate an incident lead for each incident

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Initiate execution of additional cybersecurity plans as needed to support incident response (for example, business continuity and disaster recovery)

requirements.title: Incident reports are triaged and validated

statement.text: Incident reports are triaged and validated

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Preliminarily review incident reports to confirm that they are cybersecurity-related and necessitate incident response activities

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Apply criteria to estimate the severity of an incident

requirements.title: Incidents are categorized and prioritized

statement.text: Incidents are categorized and prioritized

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Further review and categorize incidents based on the type of incident (e.g., data breach, ransomware, DDoS, account compromise)

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Prioritize incidents based on their scope, likely impact, and time-critical nature

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Select incident response strategies for active incidents by balancing the need to quickly recover from an incident with the need to observe the attacker or conduct a more thorough investigation

requirements.title: Incidents are escalated or elevated as needed

statement.text: Incidents are escalated or elevated as needed

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Track and validate the status of all ongoing incidents

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Coordinate incident escalation or elevation with designated internal and external stakeholders

requirements.title: The criteria for initiating incident recovery are applied

statement.text: The criteria for initiating incident recovery are applied

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Apply incident recovery criteria to known and assumed characteristics of the incident to determine whether incident recovery processes should be initiated

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Take the possible operational disruption of incident recovery activities into account

requirements.title: Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place during an incident and the root cause of the incident

statement.text: Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place during an incident and the root cause of the incident

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Determine the sequence of events that occurred during the incident and which assets and resources were involved in each event

examples.label: Ex2
examples.text: Attempt to determine what vulnerabilities, threats, and threat actors were directly or indirectly involved in the incident

examples.label: Ex3
examples.text: Analyze the incident to find the underlying, systemic root causes

examples.label: Ex4
examples.text: Check any cyber deception technology for additional information on attacker behavior

requirements.title: Actions performed during an investigation are recorded, and the records' integrity and provenance are preserved

statement.text: Actions performed during an investigation are recorded, and the records' integrity and provenance are preserved

examples.label: Ex1
examples.text: Require each incident responder and others (e.g., system administrators, cybersecurity engineers) who perform incident response tasks to record their actions and make the record immutable

examples.label: Ex2
